data.reasoning: The package is a standard binary distribution downloading pre-built assets from GitHub releases with pinned SHA-256 checksums. The PKGBUILD contains no malicious code, only standard variable assignments and a simple package() function. The disagreement was solely due to an API error in the first model, not a security concern.
data.disagreement_analysis: The qwen model encountered HTTP 400 errors when attempting to audit .SRCINFO and .gitignore, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully audited all files and correctly identified the package as safe.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit .SRCINFO and .gitignore due to LLM API errors (HTTP 400).
learnings: Implement retry logic or fallback mechanisms for transient LLM API errors to prevent minor file audit failures from cascading into an overall inconclusive package verdict.
Consider weighting file importance; failures on low-risk metadata files like .gitignore should not necessarily block a safe verdict if the core PKGBUILD is verified safe.
